steps: Wanted a whole Term at my own pace
Only played a 12 month Flashpoint this session

friction.expected: Read the tagline and the Flashpoint blurb
friction.happened: The globe drawn over the text; 'One clear goal' and 'Put it out, or don't' are cut across by the map edge

friction.expected: Know what the dots next to each country mean
friction.happened: Small orange/green dots with no label (difficulty? I guessed)
Seed code and 'Play this seed' are meaningless to me; Flashpoint is explained, seed is not
Mission, crisis, three cards, cabinet pick, advisors, seals, budget, meetings, orders: a lot at once. 'Seals', 'Defense budget untouched', 'Meetings' and the small caps labels were not explained
The staff had already added 'Reform program' and 'Court Germany' using up my political capital, so I had 0 left and could not do what I wanted until I found the small X
The button only focuses a plain dropdown of 41 countries with unexplained numbers in brackets (relations score). Hard to use; I gave up and used the advisor suggestion instead

friction.expected: See Russia and Ukraine to tap them
friction.happened: Globe opens on the US; Russia is off the edge, zoom out makes it tiny, and I do not drag. That was my second 'what do I press' moment

friction.expected: Ukraine news after my Ukraine-focused move
friction.happened: Headlines were 'Your forces gain ground against Iran' and 'The war with Iran is over'. I am brokering Ukraine; I did not know America was fighting Iran in my game
Candlelit protest art under 'Sell them via Germany'; handshake with Xi under 'Grant access' with no explanation of what access
'Trump chooses: Squeeze Moscow's oil buyers' repeats my own click

friction.where: Red 'FAILED' stamp on 'West Bank: worse this month'
friction.happened: Looked like my order failed; it is just the situation getting worse
'The war ended in month 3' is the Iran war, while 'The truth' page says I brokered the end of the war in month 4. Which war? Also labels truncated on the timeline
'MISSION FAILED', grade D, zero stars next to 'Master Diplomat' and 4 of 5 goals met; headline says better than 34% while card says top 66%. Score 570 of 1000 versus 115 on the desk

Sanae Takaichi (Japan PM) and Ferdinand Marcos Jr. appear as unexplained call targets; 'Iran nuclear program 15% developing', 'defence pacts', 'Pariah', 'hot zone', 'front (your side) 50 = stalemate', 'staff policy', 'simulated competent leaders' unexplained. Takaichi shown as Japan's PM with no introduction

Kit cannot zoom. At 100% the chips and small caps labels (Cabinet pick, STEP 1 of 3, seals) are already small; at 125% would be borderline fine, but some content (dashboards of arrows) would crowd and scroll more

suggestions.what: Let me tap a country name or flag on the desk to pick a target, instead of a 41 country dropdown with raw numbers
Keep the news about the conflict I chose; show the Iran or Gaza side stories in a smaller 'elsewhere' line
Do not let staff pre-spend my political capital without asking; or say in plain words at the top what they did
One sentence on the end screen: Did you succeed, and why, matching the stars and grade
Open the map centred on the countries of my mission, with a big 'Zoom to Ukraine' button
Add a short plain glossary tap on terms like seal, front, hot zone, seed

delight: The mission screen: plain goals, on track or off track (shots/ruth-laptop/006-start.png)
Order cards with 'Hurts' and 'Helps' reasons in plain words (shots/ruth-laptop/008-desk.png)
The Article 4 Poland crisis felt like the news (shots/ruth-laptop/037-d8.png)
'The truth' table: my world next to the real world with sources (shots/ruth-laptop/056-e5.png)

fun.reason: Crisis choices were absorbing and I read every one; the middle months blurred because Approve did the work.

clarity.reason: Mission screen and card reasons clear, desk crowded, and my Ukraine goal was buried under Iran and Gaza news.

visual.reason: Handsome illustrations and newspaper; globe overlapping title text on the first screen.

feels_like_a_game.reason: A story with choices; not much of a game I could try things in.

agency.reason: Staff pre-filled my orders, the country picker blocked me, and the verdict told me I failed with no plain reason.

realism.reason: Real leaders and the Poland and Hormuz details felt true; a US war with Iran and a month 3 ceasefire felt odd.

replay.reason: I would try Ukraine as Kyiv or a Term to see another outcome.

recommend.reason: I would tell a friend who reads the news, with a warning that the first screen and the orders menu need help.

quit_point: Month 2 in the All orders panel: Pick a country opened a long unexplained dropdown and I could not choose Russia; combined with the globe I would have stopped after my third what do I press moment.
verbatim: I loved reading what really happened next to my game, but why am I fighting Iran, and did I win or not?
